candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; communicate with the interprofessional team, assign/coordinate responsibilities, and implement emergency response systems
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — role clarity and standardized communication during obstetric emergencies
candidate.educational_objective: Use clearly assigned emergency roles and standardized communication to coordinate simultaneous interprofessional actions during an obstetric emergency.

options.A: Assign explicit roles and use a standardized emergency-communication process so assessment, medications, equipment, and escalation tasks are coordinated.
options.B: Allow every team member to choose tasks independently without a shared role structure because predefined responsibilities slow emergency care.
options.C: Avoid standardized communication tools during the event because structured communication increases confusion under stress.
options.D: Have only one clinician perform all urgent tasks until the diagnosis is confirmed, then involve the rest of the team.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. ACOG guidance on preparation for obstetric and gynecologic emergencies recommends protocols that designate team-member roles, drills and ongoing training, and formal standardized emergency communication such as SBAR. Clear roles and structured communication improve coordination during time-critical events and support rapid-response effectiveness. B and C remove the structure intended to reduce communication and task failures. D underuses the interprofessional response and can delay simultaneous urgent actions.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Structured obstetric emergency response should include designated roles and standardized communication so interprofessional tasks are coordinated efficiently during time-critical events.
candidate.source_document_title: Preparing for Clinical Emergencies in Obstetrics and Gynecology
